name: Clinch County School System
quote: Any administrator or certified employee designated by the principal of the Board of Education, in order to maintain proper control and discipline over pupils under his or her care and supervision, may, in the exercise of sound discretion, administer corporal punishment to any pupil or pupils under his or her care and supervision.
quotes: Any administrator or certified employee designated by the principal of the Board of Education, in order to maintain proper control and discipline over pupils under his or her care and supervision, may, in the exercise of sound discretion, administer corporal punishment to any pupil or pupils under his or her care and supervision.
The corporal punishment shall not be excessive or unduly severe.
Corporal punishment shall never be used as a first line of punishment for misbehavior unless the pupil was informed beforehand that specific misbehavior could occasion its use;
provided, however, that corporal punishment may be employed as a first line of punishment for those acts of misconduct which are so antisocial or disruptive in nature as to shock the conscience.

Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a child whose parents or legal guardian have filed with the principal of the school a statement expressly objecting to the use of corporal punishment or a statement from a medical doctor licensed in Georgia stating that corporal punishment is detrimental to the child's mental or emotional stability.
notes: Board policy JDA on Simbli, read 2026-09-25 by policy code in a sweep of Simbli sites; identity matched to the federal LEA directory by name prefix.

name: Griffin-Spalding County School System
quote: CORPORAL PUNISHMENT Corporal punishment is not permitted with the Griffin-Spalding County School System (GSCS).
quotes: CORPORAL PUNISHMENT Corporal punishment is not permitted with the Griffin-Spalding County School System (GSCS).

While the principal of each school has the authority to provide consequences to any student who violates the GSCS Student Code of Conduct, corporal punishment is not permitted as an appropriate nor permissible consequence within GSCS.

name: White County School System
quote: Any principal or other designated school administrator employed by the White County Board of Education, in order to maintain proper control and discipline over pupils under his or her care and supervision, may, in the exercise of sound discretion, administer corporal punishment to any pupil or pupils under his or her care and supervision.
quotes: Any principal or other designated school administrator employed by the White County Board of Education, in order to maintain proper control and discipline over pupils under his or her care and supervision, may, in the exercise of sound discretion, administer corporal punishment to any pupil or pupils under his or her care and supervision.

No other employee of the board or any other person, including the parents or guardian of such child or children, may administer corporal punishment in any school or on any school property in this school district.
Corporal punishment shall never be used as a first line of punishment for misbehavior unless the pupil was informed beforehand that specific misbehavior could occasion its use;
provided, however, that corporal punishment may be employed as a first line of punishment for those acts of misconduct which are so antisocial or disruptive in nature as to shock the conscience.

Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a child whose parents or legal guardian have filed with the principal of the school a statement expressly objecting to the use of corporal punishment or a statement from a medical doctor licensed in Georgia stating that corporal punishment is detrimental to the child's mental or emotional stability.

Corporal punishment shall not be administered to a student who refuses to accept corporal punishment in lieu of other punishment nor shall corporal punishment be administered to a student whose parent has requested in writing that corporal punishment not be used, regardless of whether the parent has provided a statement from a medical doctor as described above.
